entries.clue: Team players, catcalled, getting led off ground (7,6)

indicatorNotes.getting led off: something led off is walked away from where it was standing, so the letters it names leave the rest behind
indicatorNotes.ground: ground is the past tense of grind, and anything put through a mill comes out in a different arrangement

blocks.note: seven letters of fodder, taken as they stand
CATCALLED with LED taken off it, leaving six more letters of fodder

annotation.surface: Supporters jeer while a player is walked off the pitch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ground' closes the clue where a football ground would, and it is the milling instruction instead. 'Led off' is not a sending-off either: it names three letters to drop.
annotation.definitionFit: Crystal Palace is a football club in south London, so 'team' names it as plainly as a fixture list does.

entries.clue: Mars communist plot–extremist gutted (3,6)

indicatorNotes.gutted: to gut something is to take its insides out, which leaves only the letters on the outside

blocks.note: a red is a communist, after the colour of the flag
a plot is a plan, a scheme worked out in advance
the outside letters of ExtremisT

annotation.surface: A communist conspiracy with its most extreme members cut out of it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mars' sits at the front, where a capital letter proves nothing, so it reads as the verb that spoils things rather than the planet. 'Gutted' is a standard request for a word's outside only.
annotation.definitionFit: Mars looks rust-coloured through a telescope because of the iron oxide on it, and 'the red planet' is the name that stuck.

entries.clue: Frivolous cunning stopped by girl off and on (5)

indicatorNotes.stopped by: a word stopped by a caller is interrupted part of the way through, which is where the other letters go
indicatorNotes.off and on: something happening off and on happens every other time, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: sly = cunning, crafty
the second and fourth letters of gIrL

annotation.surface: A crafty scheme keeps being halted by a girl who drops in now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Off and on' takes the second and fourth letters rather than the first and third, and only the length tells you which pair is wanted. 'Stopped by' is the visiting kind of calling in the surface and an insertion underneath.
annotation.definitionFit: Frivolous and silly both describe behaviour nobody is meant to take seriously, and both are adjectives.

entries.clue: Publicity staff in trouble for one month (5)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing described as in another sits inside it, letters and all

blocks.note: pr = public relations, the department that handles publicity
to ail somebody is to trouble them

annotation.surface: The press office endures four weeks of bad news.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For one' marks what follows as a class rather than a synonym, which is how a single example can be the definition. 'Trouble' is the verb here, not the noun the surface offers.
annotation.definitionFit: April is one of the twelve months, and 'for one' is the setter admitting that the definition names the class.

entries.clue: What, when bad, could offer poor signs? (9)

annotation.definition: What, when bad, could offer poor signs?

indicatorNotes.bad: something gone bad has gone wrong, and letters gone wrong are letters no longer in the order given

blocks.note: the nine letters of fodder

annotation.surface: A question about the thing that, once it turns bad, starts showing poor indications.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds at once, so 'bad' has two jobs: it belongs to the sense being described and it is the instruction to shuffle.
annotation.definitionFit: A prognosis is a doctor's forecast of how an illness will go, so a bad one is exactly a set of poor signs.

entries.clue: Upset friend skips erotic performances (3,6)

indicatorNotes.Upset: in a down clue an upset word has been tipped over, so it reads back up the grid

blocks.note: PAL, a friend, set down backwards
to skip is to dance about lightly

annotation.surface: A distressed friend gives the strip club a miss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Skips' reads as the friend missing something and is a synonym for dancing. 'Upset' is positional rather than emotional, which only a down clue allows.
annotation.definitionFit: A lap dance is performed for one seated customer in a strip club, which is an erotic performance by any measure.

entries.clue: Box upper section of body (5)

blocks.note: a stout lidded box for blankets, tools or treasure
the front of the trunk, between neck and abdomen

annotation.surface: An instruction to punch somebody in the upper body.
annotation.walkthrough: Read as a sentence it tells you to hit a man in the ribs, and that verb reading is the whole disguise. Read as a clue it is two nouns laid side by side with no comma between them.
annotation.definitionFit: A chest is both a lidded storage box and the front of the body above the waist, two senses of one word.

entries.clue: Bright and vigorous cook going around Asia dashes about (5,2,1,5)

indicatorNotes.going around: a thing going around another encircles it, so it splits to let the rest sit inside
indicatorNotes.about: letters sent about are sent every which way, and need not come back in the order they left

blocks.note: to fry is to cook, and the word opens up to take the rest inside
the ten letters of ASIA DASHES redealt

annotation.surface: A cook tours Asia at speed, dashing from one place to the next.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Going around' and 'about' are two separate instructions, one to wrap and one to jumble, though the surface reads both as the same restless travelling. A three-letter wrapper can break two letters in front and one behind.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone fresh as a daisy is rested, wide awake and full of go, which is what bright and vigorous describes.

entries.clue: Disrespect pro, shattering team spirit (6,2,5)

indicatorNotes.shattering: a shattered thing lies in pieces, and pieces can be picked up in any order at all

blocks.note: the thirteen letters of fodder

annotation.surface: Insulting a professional wrecks the mood of the whole side.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface says what the answer denies, since disrespecting a teammate really does shatter the thing being defined. The phrase is French taken whole, and it keeps its French spelling.
annotation.definitionFit: Esprit de corps is the shared pride and loyalty that binds a group, which plain English calls team spirit.

entries.clue: Comic villain, one poking holes? (7)

blocks.note: the Batman adversary who leaves puzzles behind at his crimes
to riddle a thing is to pierce it all over, so the agent noun follows

annotation.surface: A cartoon bad guy who goes about punching holes in things.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense is the older one: a riddle is a coarse sieve, and to riddle something is to leave it full of holes. Both halves are nouns, which is the join a double definition needs.
annotation.definitionFit: The Riddler is the puzzle-setting villain of the Batman comics, and a riddler is separately anyone who riddles a thing with holes.

entries.clue: Shore up tipsy old poet and musician (7)

indicatorNotes.tipsy: somebody tipsy is unsteady on their feet, and letters in that state will not stand where they were put

blocks.note: the seven letters of fodder

annotation.surface: Propping up an unsteady old poet and musician.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shore up' looks like the verb of the sentence, the thing being done to the drunk, and it is the fodder. 'Tipsy' reads as description of him and is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Orpheus was the supreme poet and lyre-player, whose music moved rocks and charmed the dead.

entries.clue: Small trifle spread out (5)

blocks.note: s = small, the clothes-label abbreviation
to trifle with something is to play with it

annotation.surface: A modest pudding laid out along the table.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trifle' is the verb meaning to dally, not the sponge and custard the surface serves, and 'spread out' is the definition rather than more of the table setting.
annotation.definitionFit: To splay is to spread apart, the way fingers or the legs of a tripod do.

entries.clue: Earl animatedly welcomes northern actors in royal house (9)

indicatorNotes.animatedly: anything done animatedly is done with lively movement, and letters moved about lively do not land where they started
indicatorNotes.welcomes: a host who welcomes guests takes them inside, so what follows goes within

blocks.note: the four letters of EARL redealt, then opened up to take the rest
n = northern, the standard abbreviation
the cast is the company of actors in a production

annotation.surface: A peer enthusiastically greets a troupe of actors up from the north.
annotation.walkthrough: A royal house is a dynasty, not a building, and the one wanted here fought the Wars of the Roses under the red rose. 'Animatedly' is a quiet anagram word: lively movement, applied to letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Lancaster was the royal line of Henry IV, V and VI, one of the two houses whose quarrel became the Wars of the Roses.

entries.clue: Scrap book, with second article removed (5)

indicatorNotes.removed: a thing removed is taken out and not put back, so the word loses that letter for good

blocks.note: an annual is the book that comes out once a year
ANNUAL carries the indefinite article A twice, and the second of them goes

annotation.surface: A scrapbook with one of its cuttings taken out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scrap book' reads as one word on the surface and splits into definition and wordplay. 'Article' is the grammarian's word, which is how a single letter hides behind it.
annotation.definitionFit: To annul a marriage or a contract is to scrap it, declaring that it never held in the first place.

entries.clue: Painting captures headland (9)

blocks.note: to land a fish or a contract is to capture it
a cape is a headland running out into the sea

annotation.surface: A picture catching a headland on canvas.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Captures' sits exactly where a container instruction would sit and is a plain synonym instead, since nothing in this clue goes inside anything. Three words, and two of them are wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A landscape is a painting of open country, the genre taking its name from what it shows.

entries.clue: Master of Arts thus runs away from Saviour, one who embraces suffering (9)

indicatorNotes.away from: to take something away from a word is to leave it short by those letters

blocks.note: the initials of the degree
so = thus, therefore
CHRIST losing R, the cricket scorer's letter for runs

annotation.surface: An arts graduate accordingly bolts away from the Saviour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Runs' is the scorecard's R waiting to be taken out, not a verb of fleeing, and that one word is what lets the whole surface read as an escape.
annotation.definitionFit: A masochist takes pleasure in pain, so the definition describes the taste rather than offering a synonym.

entries.clue: Young person is able to head off southern islanders (9)

indicatorNotes.head off: the head of a word is the letter it begins with, and here that letter comes off to be used on its own

blocks.note: a minor is somebody under the age of majority
can = is able to
the head of Southern, detached

annotation.surface: A youngster manages to fend off some islanders from the south.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like fending something away and asks instead for a first letter to be detached. The definition is the final word on its own, which is as little as a clue can give you.
annotation.definitionFit: Minorca, the Balearic island east of Majorca, has Minorcans living on it — the English spelling of Menorca keeps the I.

entries.clue: Chuck following one to north London borough (9)

indicatorNotes.following: a piece that follows another is set down after it, so the throwing word comes second

blocks.note: i = one, the Roman numeral
to chuck something is to sling it
the word is spelt out for its own two letters
n = north, the standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A throw aimed after somebody on the road to a borough in north London.
annotation.walkthrough: 'North London' is how the surface wants to be read, and the split falls between them: the N is wordplay and London alone is definition. 'To' is spelt out rather than translated.
annotation.definitionFit: Islington is one of the thirty-two London boroughs, covering Angel and Highbury just north of the City.

entries.clue: Roman emperor into Annus Horribilis? (9)

indicatorNotes.Horribilis: the Latin for horrible, and a word in a horrible state is one with its letters in disarray

blocks.note: the nine letters of fodder, the preposition included

annotation.surface: A Roman emperor dropped into a truly dreadful year.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Annus horribilis' is the Queen's own phrase for her dreadful 1992, and the italics flag it as Latin. 'Into' poses as the word joining two halves of a clue, and its four letters are needed.
annotation.definitionFit: Antoninus Pius ruled Rome from 138 to 161, and the name was carried by several later emperors as well.

entries.clue: Victor interrupts only what you’re now trying to do? (5)

annotation.definition: what you’re now trying to do?

indicatorNotes.interrupts: to interrupt is to cut in part of the way through, which is where the letter lands

blocks.note: sole = only, the single one
v for Victor in the radio alphabet

annotation.surface: A man called Victor butts in on the one job you have in hand.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition points at the reader rather than at anything in the world, a wink setters allow themselves about once a puzzle. Victor is the radio alphabet's name for a letter, not a winner.
annotation.definitionFit: Working a clue out is solving it, so the definition simply describes what the reader is doing at that moment.

entries.clue: Dicky ran castle of forebears (9)

indicatorNotes.Dicky: dicky is British for shaky or unsound — a dicky knee, a dicky heart — and nothing unsound holds its shape

blocks.note: the nine letters of fodder

annotation.surface: A man called Dicky who used to run a castle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' passes for a name standing in front of a verb, helped by the capital that begins every clue and proves nothing. In British use it means unsound or unreliable.
annotation.definitionFit: Ancestral means belonging to one's forebears, as an ancestral home or an ancestral right does.

entries.clue: Company adopts radical belief (5)

indicatorNotes.adopts: a family that adopts takes somebody into itself, so those letters go inside

blocks.note: co = company, as on a firm's letterhead
a red is a political radical of the left

annotation.surface: A firm takes on a left-winger.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Radical' is a noun here, and red has stood for that politics since long before the Russian revolution. The definition is the last word by itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of belief — Latin for 'I believe', and the name of the creed sung at Mass.

entries.clue: Fine cotton left on edges of inlays and lace (5)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue whatever sits on something else rests above it, so that piece is written first
indicatorNotes.edges of: the edges of a word are its first and last letters, everything between them falling away

blocks.note: l = left, the standard abbreviation
the first and last of Inlay S
the same edges taken again, from Lac E

annotation.surface: Cotton lies along the trimmed borders of some inlaid work and lace.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Edges of' reaches across the 'and' to serve both words, a shortcut that saves the setter repeating an instruction. 'Left' is the single letter, not a past tense of leaving.
annotation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine smooth cotton thread used for stockings and gloves, named after Lisle, the old English spelling of Lille.

entries.clue: Fruit that stuffs German goose (5)

indicatorNotes.stuffs: whatever stuffs a bird is packed away inside it, out of sight

blocks.note: GerMAN GOose carries it across the gap between the words

annotation.surface: A fruit used as the stuffing for a goose from Germany.
annotation.walkthrough: The join between two words is the hardest hiding place to see, because the eye insists on reading whole words. 'Stuffs' is both the hiding instruction and part of the cookery.
annotation.definitionFit: A mango is the sweet tropical stone fruit, so 'fruit' names it as flatly as a greengrocer would.

entries.clue: Leaders among men of letters analyse rates that may be capped (5)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition describes rather than names: it is a relative clause standing in for the noun, and the setter is entitled to it because only one sort of thing is meant.

indicatorNotes.Leaders among: the leader of a word is the letter standing at its head, and the clue wants one from each word that follows

blocks.note: the opening letters of Men Of Letters Analyse Rates

annotation.surface: Writers go through figures that might have a ceiling put on them.
annotation.walkthrough: Capped rates are the surface's business, a limit on what can be charged, while the capping meant is a dentist's. 'Men of letters' reads as one phrase for writers and is really five words in a row.
annotation.definitionFit: A damaged tooth is given a crown, commonly called a cap, and a molar is the back grinding tooth that most often needs one.

entries.clue: Composer worked at Mensa (7)

indicatorNotes.worked: dough that is worked is kneaded into a new shape, and letters take the same treatment

blocks.note: the seven letters of fodder

annotation.surface: A composer holds down a job at the high-IQ society.
annotation.walkthrough: Mensa is the society for people scoring in the top two per cent on an IQ test, which is what lets the clue pass as a sentence about a clever man. 'Worked' is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana was the nineteenth-century Czech composer of Má vlast and The Bartered Bride.

entries.clue: Separate tips of spark plugs illuminated (5,2)

indicatorNotes.tips of: a word's tip is the letter it starts with, and each word named here gives one up

blocks.note: the leading letters of Spark Plugs
lit up = illuminated

annotation.surface: Spark plugs glowing at their points.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is one uninterrupted piece of engine talk, with both halves of the wordplay tucked inside it. 'Illuminated' hands over two words rather than one, which the enumeration quietly warns you about.
annotation.definitionFit: To split up is to separate, whether a couple parting or a group dividing into smaller ones.

entries.clue: Accessory that facilitates change of direction in estate? (5,8)

annotation.definition: Accessory that facilitates change of direction in estate?

blocks.clueFragment: Accessory that facilitates change of direction
blocks.note: on the surface this is any fitting that helps something take a new course, which is how the sentence asks to be read
an estate is also an estate car, and the question mark is the setter admitting that the accessory comes on every other model too

annotation.surface: A fitting that helps a landed estate change the direction it is going in.
annotation.walkthrough: Nothing here breaks into letters: no fodder, no indicator, no container. The lever is 'estate', which the surface wants as land and property and the setter means as a car with a long back.
annotation.definitionFit: Power steering uses the engine to turn the front wheels, so it is precisely the accessory that makes changing direction easy in a car.
